dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I've noted some changes in your behavior and eating habits recently; could you tell me when you first started noticing these shifts?
I don't really care about the timing, but do you have any snacks in this office? I was hoping for some chocolate pudding or maybe some chips while we sit here. You have a very shiny tie, by the way.
Thank you for the compliment on my tie. Have your friends or family mentioned that you've been acting differently in social situations or being more blunt than usual lately?

My family is always complaining about something, but I find them quite boring these days to be honest. I’d much rather go find that pretty woman in the waiting room and give her a big kiss. Do you think she'd like that?

I understand you're feeling quite impulsive right now, but let's stay focused on your health. Have you noticed yourself repeating certain actions or words frequently, or feeling a strong need to follow a very strict routine?

I don't bother with routines, they're too much work and I'd rather just do what I want. Why are you asking so many questions instead of getting me those snacks? You've got a funny way of talking, has anyone ever told you that?

I apologize for the wait on the snacks; I'll see what we can find shortly. Have you or your family noticed any new difficulties with your memory or finding the right words during conversations? 

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

It is helpful to know that your memory remains sharp, though I am concerned about these changes in your social filter and appetite. Have you or your family noticed any history of similar personality changes or dementia in your

I don't know why they'd be worried, I feel perfectly fine and just want to enjoy my pudding. My family can be so dramatic, but I honestly haven't been paying much attention to what they say. Is that a bowl of candy on your desk, or can I go see if that lady is still outside?

I see the candy is tempting, but let's talk more about your family; do you find it harder to understand how they feel or care about their concerns lately?

REQUEST TEST: PET_Scan_Brain
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
Since your brain scans came back normal, I would like to look closer at your daily habits. Have you found yourself craving sweets like pudding much more than usual lately, and have you had

I already told you I want the pudding, and I've put on quite a bit of weight because it's all I want to eat lately. I can't help it if chips and sweets are the only things that taste good anymore. Are you going to keep talking, or can I go find something to munch on?
I understand your focus is on the snacks right now. Have you noticed a loss of interest in hobbies you used to enjoy, or do you find it difficult to manage your finances and daily tasks?

I don't see the point in those old hobbies anymore, they're just not interesting. I haven't looked at my bank stuff in months because it's much more fun to just focus on what I'm eating. Can we wrap this up so I can go get some more potato chips?

I appreciate your patience. Have you or your family noticed any changes in your physical movements, such as stiffness, tremors, or difficulty walking?

    Wait, the dialogue limit is 1-3

I move just fine, though I suppose I don't get up much unless there's food involved. My legs work well enough to walk over and talk to that girl in the hallway, so I'm not worried about stiffness. Why are you asking about my walking when there aren't even any chips in this room yet?

I understand you're eager for those chips. Have you been sleeping more than usual, or perhaps finding that you have an unusual amount of energy throughout the night? 

REQUEST TEST: Neuropsych

RESULTS: Mental status examination reveals apathy and blunted affect. The patient avoids answering questions. Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28/30. Physical neurological examination is unremarkable.

Thank you for your patience during this examination. Given your symptoms of behavioral disinhibition, apathy, and significant dietary changes alongside your test results, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS
A conclusion? That sounds like a lot of talking that isn't bringing me any chocolate pudding. I don't really care what you call it, as long as I can finally leave and find something to eat.

I appreciate your patience while we discussed your health. Based on your behavioral changes, social disinhibition, apathy, and strong preference for sweets, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOS
Look, you’re still talking and I still don't have any chips. I don't care about a "conclusion" or whatever you're about to say. Can I go now?
